title: 'Atualizar baseline' promises grave security findings cannot be baselined, but check_grants.mjs writes anon write grants and RLS-off into the baseline and silences the daily gate
description: The dispatch-only workflow `Atualizar baseline` (contents/pull-requests write) is the documented mobile path to update scripts/security_baseline.json through a PR. Its header (atualizar-baseline.yml:19-21) states that, by design of the script, it cannot baseline one of the six grave indicators: check_grants.mjs refuses and exits 1 before writing. The PR body it generates (line 159) repeats this to the owner who decides the merge. The script has no such refusal: check_grants.mjs:158-170 writes every severity-'erro' finding, including grant_escrita (anon/authenticated INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE), rls_off, policy_escrita and funcao_public_execute, then exits 0. Once that PR is merged, the daily `seguranca` job (db-checks.yml:144), which ADR-0003 calls the control that protects the database, treats the live grave state as a known exception and passes. The realistic trigger is documented: supabase_admin default privileges grant anon write on new public tables and cannot be closed (db-checks.yml:13-17).
root_cause: The --atualizar-baseline branch of check_grants.mjs filters only on severity ('erro') and has no deny-list of non-baselinable finding types. The read side (lines 173-186) likewise accepts any baselined key, so neither the workflow nor a hand-edited baseline can be stopped from silencing grave findings. The workflow and PR text assert a control that git history shows never existed.
intended_behavior: `check_grants.mjs --atualizar-baseline` must exit 1 without writing when any grave indicator is present (anon/authenticated write or MAINTAIN grants, RLS off, non-SELECT policies that do not block writes, PUBLIC-executable functions, permissive default privileges outside the documented supabase_admin limitation). The normal gate must never treat those types as known exceptions, as atualizar-baseline.yml:19-21 and :159 promise.

trace.description: A writer, or the agent acting for the phone-only owner, dispatches the baseline update to clear a red `seguranca` gate.
Runs `node scripts/check_grants.mjs --atualizar-baseline` against the live database through the auditor credential.
Live anon write grants become `grant_escrita` findings with the default severity 'erro'. rls_off (line 111), policy_escrita (line 129) and funcao_public_execute (line 135) are built the same way.
The only filter is `a.severidade === 'erro'`. Every grave finding is serialized and written to scripts/security_baseline.json (line 167), and the process exits 0 (line 170).

trace.scope: steps['Abrir o PR com o diff'] gh pr create --body
trace.description: The PR body tells the merging owner 'Os seis indicadores graves não passam por aqui — o script recusa baseliná-los e sai 1 antes de escrever', which is false.
After merge, the baselined grave keys count as `conhecidos`, `novos` is empty and the gate exits 0 ('nenhum achado novo') while anon can still write.

evidence.description: Claimed control: 'baselinar um dos SEIS indicadores graves. `check_grants.mjs` recusa e sai 1 antes de escrever ... Este workflow não tem como contornar isso, e é de propósito.'
The --atualizar-baseline block writes all severity-'erro' findings with no type-based refusal. A git -G search across all refs finds no grave-indicator logic in scripts/ ever.
Daily cadence exists because supabase_admin default privileges grant anon write and cannot be closed, which is the expected source of a live grave finding.
'Sigilo não é o que protege o banco aqui; o gate diário é.' The silenced gate is the stated protective control.

conditions.description: A grave posture exists live in the sole Supabase database (e.g. a public table anon can INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, as supabase_admin default privileges produce), so the daily seguranca gate is red.
A repository writer or workflow dispatcher (the owner, or the agent the docs designate to run Actions for the phone-only owner) runs 'Atualizar baseline' with baseline=seguranca.
The owner merges the generated PR, relying on its body's assertion that grave indicators cannot be included.

execution.attacker_perspective: A lower-trust state change (an anon-writable public table appearing live, for example via the unclosable supabase_admin default privileges) meets the documented 'Atualizar baseline' path. The workflow output, not a reviewer's own analysis, tells the owner the grave state could not have been baselined.
payloads: Fake psql response for the security shape: tabela_vista_teste anon {select,insert,update,delete,truncate}=true with a PERMISSIVE 'w' policy qual/with_check 'true'; evento_dados rls=false; divat_api_shape() public_execute=true, security_definer=true, search_path_fixo=false; postgres default privilege on public tables anon=INSERT
instructions: Copy scripts/check_grants.mjs, scripts/lib/audit-database.mjs, scripts/lib/security-policies.mjs and scripts/security_baseline.json into an empty scratch directory with the same scripts/ layout (same approach as tests/check_grants.rig.mjs).
Put a fake `psql` first on PATH that prints the grave security-shape fixture as one JSON line. Set the dummy auditor URL. Run with no network.
Run `node scripts/check_grants.mjs` and record the exit status. Run it again with `--atualizar-baseline`, then once more in normal mode against the same fixture.
Read the scripts/security_baseline.json the second run wrote.
execution.observed_result: Normal gate before: exit 1, '✗ POSTURA DE SEGURANÇA REGREDIU', listing [grant_escrita] anon tem INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE em tabela_vista_teste, [policy_escrita], [rls_off] RLS desligada em evento_dados and [funcao_public_execute]. --atualizar-baseline: exit 0, '✓ Baseline reescrito com 7 exceção(ões)'. The baseline now contains grant_escrita tabela_vista_teste:anon, policy_escrita tabela_vista_teste:anon_write_all, rls_off evento_dados and funcao_public_execute divat_api_shape(). Normal gate after: exit 0, '✓ Postura de segurança: nenhum achado novo', with the same grave state listed as known exceptions (agents/h17-ci-secrets/artifacts/check-01.out).

remediation.strategy: Implement the promised refusal in check_grants.mjs on both sides. On write, --atualizar-baseline exits 1 without writing when any grave type is present. On read, grave types in the baseline file are never honored, so a hand-edited baseline cannot silence them either. Keep the documented supabase_admin default-privilege and rls_auto_enable() exceptions baselinable. Add rig cases to tests/check_grants.rig.mjs: (a) --atualizar-baseline with anon INSERT → exit 1 and baseline byte-identical; (b) a baseline containing grant_escrita → gate still exits 1. Until then, correct atualizar-baseline.yml:19-21 and :159 so the PR does not assert a non-existent guard.

likelihood.reason: Requires a live grave posture, a deliberate dispatch of the baseline workflow and a human merge. The red gate and the documented phone-only path make that sequence plausible, and the PR text actively tells the reviewer the grave case is impossible.

impact.reason: An anon-writable or RLS-off table on the sole production database would stay live with the daily gate green. The gate is the stated protective control (ADR-0003), and the impact on data integrity is the anonymous writes it no longer reports.

confidence.reason: The source shows no refusal anywhere in history, and a sandboxed run of the real script copies with a dummy credential reproduced baseline write, exit 0 and a silenced gate.
